name: Small strain Timoshenko cantilever bending, ten elements

source.originalStudy: Prathap and Bhashyam (1982), International Journal for Numerical Methods in Engineering, volume 18, pages 195–210

case.model: straight cantilever, clamped at x=0, transverse tip load in local y

limitations: The source page's displayed analytical deflection exponent is inconsistent with its separately reported ten-element finite-element result. This check compares only with the published finite-element result.

The public TimoshenkoBeam3D implementation provides an element stiffness matrix, not a beam-mesh assembler. The verification harness assembles the documented straight, uniform mesh and uses the production sparse solver.

The source does not report torsional constant J. The harness supplies a positive explicit value for the uncoupled torsion block; the checked y-plane response is independent of J for this linear model.
This is experimental cross-solver correlation for one linear beam case. It does not establish beam workflow validation, mesh convergence, or release maturity.
